# 1 Enoch Chapter 66 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**1** From there I was taken to another place. To the west he showed me another enormous mountain of solid, hard rock.

**2** Cut into it were four great hollows — deep and wide and perfectly smooth. The smoothness of them, the depth, and the darkness when you looked in were striking.

**3** Then Raphael, one of the holy angels accompanying me, spoke up and explained: "These hollows were made for exactly this purpose: so that the spirits of the souls of the dead could gather here — yes, all the souls of every human being will come here. These places have been prepared to hold them until the day of their judgment, until their appointed time — until the great judgment comes upon them."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Ch. 66 interrupts the Parables with a vision of the intermediate state — the place where the dead wait for judgment. Raphael's explanation answers the question of what happens between death and the final judgment. The four hollow places may correspond to the four categories of the dead in 1 En 22 (righteous; sinners who will be judged; murdered victims; those who died without judgment in life).*
